I have been working in clinical research for over three years, beginning my career as a Clinical Trial Assistant (CTA) before transitioning to the CRA role in December 2025. During my time as a CTA, I have developed a strong understanding of study operations, data management and cross-functional collaboration, skills that have provided a solid foundation for my current role. What is the best part of your job? One of the things I enjoy most about clinical research is the opportunity to contribute to the development of new medical advances while continuously learning from the people around me. Clinical trials are truly a team effort, involving investigators, coordinators, sponsors, participants and many other professionals. Supporting sites through planning, communication and problem-solving while helping maintain participant safety and data quality is both rewarding and meaningful to me. What has been interesting about your work in clinical research? Did anything surprise you about the patient population? One experience that has stayed with me was working on a HPV vaccine study. I was surprised by how engaged many of the healthy volunteers were. Rather than simply receiving information during the informed consent process, many participants arrived with their own knowledge, asked thoughtful questions and showed a genuine interest in understanding the research. Their enthusiasm and commitment to contributing to medical progress left a lasting impression on me. What are you most proud of in your work? I am proud of my ability to bring people together and solve challenges through effective communication. Whether it is helping stakeholders align on complex contract discussions or working proactively with sites to accelerate ethics committee submissions and approvals, I enjoy finding ways to improve efficiency and keep studies moving forward. Seeing a site activate ahead of schedule because of strong collaboration across teams is especially rewarding. For me, success is not only about achieving project milestones, but also about building strong relationships and helping everyone work towards a shared goal. I'm excited to continue growing in clinical research at Fortrea, learning from every study and collaboration, and contributing to research that has the potential to improve patient care and advance medical knowledge. Their commitment is inspiring and serves as a constant reminder that behind every protocol, data point and study milestone are real people placing their trust in clinical research. What are you most proud of in your work? I am most proud of the moments when a study reaches an important milestone. Clinical trials require significant planning, coordination and collaboration over many years. Whether it is site activation, enrollment completion, database lock, or overall study completion, each achievement represents meaningful progress toward bringing innovative treatments to patients. Being part of that journey is what continues to motivate me and reinforces the importance of the work we do every day. How long have you been working in the area of clinical research? I have been working in clinical research for eight years, including the past five years with Fortrea, supporting studies across all regions of China. Throughout my career, I have had the opportunity to work on a wide range of clinical trial projects, gaining experience across different therapeutic areas and collaborating with investigators, study teams and healthcare professionals nationwide. What is the best part of your job? What I enjoy most about my role as a Clinical Research Associate is the opportunity to contribute throughout the entire lifecycle of a clinical trial. My work includes preparing sites for study initiation, coordinating with investigators, overseeing trial procedures, conducting monitoring visits, verifying source data, and following up on study-related issues. While much of the role requires careful attention to detail and strong process management, I find it incredibly rewarding because every activity contributes to the quality and integrity of the research. Over the years, this work has strengthened my communication, problem-solving and critical thinking skills, while also teaching me the importance of precision, accountability and collaboration. What has been interesting about your work in clinical research? Did anything surprise you about the patient population? One of the most fascinating aspects of clinical research is that it is a profession built on continuous learning. Every study presents an opportunity to deepen my understanding of medical science, drug development and industry regulations. I have worked alongside experienced investigators, physicians and healthcare teams, gaining valuable insights into how clinical research is translated into real-world medical practice. The dynamic nature of the field means there is always something new to learn, whether it is an innovative treatment approach, an emerging therapeutic area or an evolving regulatory requirement. What are you most proud of in your work? What I am most proud of is maintaining a strong commitment to quality throughout every study I support. Clinical trial data must be accurate, complete and compliant, as these factors are essential to protecting patients and advancing scientific knowledge. In my daily work, I carefully review data, follow up on issues, assess potential risks and work closely with investigators and site teams to help ensure studies progress smoothly. I take pride in knowing that my attention to detail helps contribute to the reliability of clinical research and supports the development of new treatments. Perhaps the most meaningful part of my work is knowing that clinical trials have the potential to improve patients' lives. Being able to contribute, even in a small way, to the journey of a medicine from clinical development to real-world use is something I never take for granted.
